chapter_theme: Samipam, nearness to the Lord, set in a ladder of the four states by what becomes of the bond (பாசம்) in each, until in sayujyam the bond dissolves and the Lord alone remains.

1509.reading: In salokam the bond is still the soul's; in samipam the bond turns into grace; in sarupam the bond becomes the crown; with the bond dissolved, the Lord is sayujyam.
1509.nuance: Each line turns on what பாசம் becomes: பசுவானது (of the soul, or the soul's own state), அருளானது (grace), சிரமானது (the head or crown; possibly 'toilsome', or a corrupt word), and கரை (dissolves, or reaches its shore). The scheme uses the three Siddhanta categories, pati, pasu and pasam, to rank the states; the exact sense of each line is the tradition's.

links.note: 1507 matches the states of release to the paths; 1509 ranks the same states by what happens to the bond in each, ending in its dissolving.

source_issues: 1509: சிரமானது in line 3 is unclear and may be corrupt.
